Judgment:

(Per Hon'ble Sri Justice Vakiti Ramakrishna Reddy) This Appeal Suit is filed by the appellant/respondent/plaintiffs against the Order and Decree dated 19.04.2022 passed in I.A.No.306 of 2022 in O.S.No.55 of 2021 on the file of the I Additional Chief Judge, City Civil Court at Secunderabad, wherein the suit filed by the plaintiff against the defendant was rejected on the application filed by the defendant.

sentences.text: 2. For the sake of convenience, the parties will be referred as per their status before the trial Court.

I. BRIEF FACTS:
3. The plaintiffs filed suit vide O.S.No.55 of 2021 seeking declaration and perpetual injunction in respect of suit schedule property i.e., land admeasuring Ac.40.00 guntas in GLR Sy.No.243 situated in Cantonment Area, Secunderabad against the sole defendant in pursuance of the liberty granted in W.A. No.150/2021 and directions issued by this Court, as well as earlier proceedings including W.P.
No.5049/2016.

The dispute pertains to property held for over 75 years, with both sides submitting substantial AKS,J & VRKR,J CCCA_49_2022 documentary records and referencing specific Court orders and dates for previous proceedings.
The parties have approached the Court seeking adjudication of title, possession, and compliance with legal and procedural directions.

4. During the pendency of the suit, the defendant filed a petition vide I.A.No.306 of 2022 in O.S.No.55 of 2021 for rejection of the plaint by invoking Order VII Rule 11 read with Sections 35-A and 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure.

sentences.text:
The brief averments of the affidavit filed in support of the said petition are as under:
a) The defendant asserts that their family acquired and possessed the disputed property peacefully for over 75 years, as reflected in the documents dated as far back as 1955 and subsequent years, with government registration and mutation records supporting their continuous title.

The suit is filed based on an entry in the GLR only which was allegedly prepared in the year 1945 and the land claimed by the plaintiffs is shown as B2 land and as per the plaintiffs' own contentions, B2 land covers private land also.

The name of the predecessors-in-title was recorded in the revenue record prior to independence and after independence, the State itself prepared Sethwar in the year 1950 and Khasra Pahani in the year AKS,J & VRKR,J CCCA_49_2022 1954-55 after survey, proper inquiry, which carries a presumption of genuinity.

b) There is no pleading in the plaint or document filed along with the plaint to show that for the past 76 years, the State acted as owner or initiated any steps against the The State Of Telangana And 3 Others vs M/S.Shantha Sriram Constructions ... on 7 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/156916124/
3 defendant without the prescribed period of limitation.

sentences.text: Therefore, the relief of declaration of title on a reading of the plaint itself cannot be countenanced and the same is hopelessly barred by limitation.

c) The relief of cancellation of registered documents of title of the defendant and its predecessors-in-title which have been in existence since 1955 and 2006 has no legs to stand, since no such dispute was ever raised by the plaintiffs at any point of time.

The Plaintiff State being the registering authority and having collected the stamp duty and registration charges, cannot claim ignorance for more than 65 years and 15 years respectively, more so without there being any specific pleading with regard to the same.
d) The act of acquiring part of land from the predecessors-in-title of the petitioner is admitted in the plaint.

This demonstrates clear knowledge of the plaintiff State as the very same revenue and Cantonment officials AKS,J & VRKR,J CCCA_49_2022 initiated the proceedings, acquired the land and paid compensation to Seth Kishan Ram Gowli., the ancestor through whom the owners who executed the Development Agreement cum General Power of Attorney (DGPA) in favour of the defendant.

Thus,
from the date of initiation of land acquisition proceedings, the suit for such relief of cancellation or declaration, should have been filed within three years under Article 58 of the Limitation Act.
When the right to sue in relation to a suit is based on multiple causes of action, the period of limitation will begin to run from the date when the right to sue first accrues.
In this regard, the defendant relied upon decisions of the Honourable Supreme Court in Prem Singh and others v. Birbal and others 1 and Ramti Devi v. Union of India 2.

sentences.text: e) The suit is filed in violation of directions issued by this Court in W.P.No.5049 of 2016 and it is also admitted in the plaint that this Court directed the plaintiff State to file a suit for declaration of title and seek the relief of recovery of possession not only against the defendant but also against its predecessors-in-title
, however, the suit is not filed against the defendant's predecessors-in-title.
Thus, the suit is not only bad in law for non joinder of necessary parties but also in utter disregard to the orders of this Court.

A reading of the plant shows that though the reliefs are sought for cancellation of the documents of 1955 and 2006, the cause of action as specified in the suit allegedly commences from 2013 and there is absolutely no correlation for the reliefs sought with the cause of action and there is no subsisting cause of action which has been pleaded in the plaint and therefore, there is no cause of action for maintaining the suit.

g) The Plaintiff State admitted in paragraph 10 of the plaint that there was land acquisition award passed in favour of Seth Kishan Ram Gowli for more than 30 years ago and the said award remained The State Of Telangana And 3 Others vs M/S.Shantha Sriram Constructions ... on 7 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/156916124/
4 unchallenged.

sentences.text: Thus, the Plaintiff State after having passed the Award more than 30 years ago is barred from making a collateral challenge to the same in the suit.
The Plaintiff State suppressed material facts and therefore, the plaint is not maintainable in law.

When the conduct of the Plaintiff State or its agents, has been such as to disentitle them from the assistance of the Court as per Section 41 (f) of the Specific Relief Act, 1963, the Plaintiff State is not entitled for equitable relief of injunction and as such, the plaint is barred by law and does not disclose any subsisting cause of action.

5. The Respondent No.4/plaintiff No.4 filed counter alleging that limitation is a mixed question of law and fact and prima facie, the plaintiff had explained in the pleadings that the suit filed well within prescribed AKS,J & VRKR,J CCCA_49_2022 period of limitation and with regard to cause of action, the plaintiff had elaborately explained various material facts which constitute the cause of action for filing the suit.
Both the aspects have to be decided after due course of trial through oral and documentary evidence.
Lack of jurisdiction is not a ground for rejection of the plaint and it can be decided after the trial is concluded.

III. FINDINGS OF THE TRIAL COURT:
6. Upon consideration of the rival contentions, the Trial Court allowed the I.A.No.306 of 2022, by rejecting the plaint in O.S.No.55 of 2021, by Order and decree dated 19/04/2022.

Consequentially,
the interim orders of status-quo initially granted in I.A.No.955/2021 dated 04.10.2021, was ordered to be vacated, and the issue was conclusively answered in favour of the petitioner/defendant.
7. Aggrieved thereby, the plaintiffs preferred the present Appeal to set aside the impugned order.
IV. SUBMISSIONS OF THE PARTIES:
A) Submissions on behalf of the appellant/plaintiff:
8.

The learned Special Government Pleader representing the Advocate General, appearing for the plaintiffs contends that Trial Court committed AKS,J & VRKR,J CCCA_49_2022 grave error in grossly ignoring the judicial precedents upholding and reiterating the principle that when the plaintiff pleads, vide the averments in the plaint, that the cause of action is actuated by fraud, the plaint cannot be rejected without affording the requisite opportunity to both the parties to adduce the necessary evidence in that regard.

9. The learned Special Government Pleader further contends that the Trial Court grossly erred in referring and countenancing with the pleadings made in the written statement as well as the petition filed under Order VII Rule 11 of the CPC, and the other documents referred thereto, including the observations of this Court in W.P.No.5049/2016 and W.A. No. 150/2021, dated 08.03.2021 and 02.07.2021 respectively, though the said records/observations did not form part of the pleadings in the plaint.

The Trial Court grossly erred in not properly appreciating the pleadings in the plaint, the material documents/records produced on behalf of the plaintiff in that regard, as well as various judgments of the Honourable Apex Court in substantiation of maintainability of the suit, succinctly The State Of Telangana And 3 Others vs M/S.Shantha Sriram Constructions ... on 7 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/156916124/

The Trial Court ought to have seen that the broad principles laid down by the Honourable Apex Court, vide various judgments, that the trial courts should refrain themselves from considering any evidence or entering into a disputed question of fact and law by departing or ignoring the pleadings raised and the documents appended to the plaint.
AKS,J & VRKR,J CCCA_49_2022 11.

It is further submitted that the Trial Court grossly erred in not verifying and appreciating the number of documents filed along with the plaint, more than 13 documents, the contents whereunder have unequivocally established the right, title and interest of the appellant/plaintiffs over the suit schedule property in respect of which, the appellant/Plaintiffs have time and again asserted and established its indefeasible and unfettered rights as owners, by issuing necessary Government Orders (G.O.'s) right from the year 1996 and initiating appropriate proceedings as against A.P.Wakf Board & others in various forums including the Wakf Tribunal and the High Court, culminating in crystallization and reiteration of the indefeasible rights as owner i.e., State, over the suit schedule property which is comprised in GLR Sy.No.243.
12.

The learned Special Government Pleader further argued that the learned Trial Court erred in not referring/mentioning about the above referred voluminous evidence by conveniently omitting to mention in the impugned order and restricting by mentioning that from the digital extract of GLR register, no other document has been referred to in the plaint to show that the respondent/Plaintiffs i.e., State exercised its right as owners of the suit land from 1945 to till date of passing orders under AP Land Encroachment Act by the Tahsildar, Tirumalgiri on 05.12.2013.

The Trial AKS,J & VRKR,J CCCA_49_2022 Court admittedly committed grave error by recording the extract of observation contained in Para No.97 in the order dated 08.03.2021 in W.P.No. 5049 of 2016 and concluding that Appellant/Plaintiffs being the custodian of the records, cannot take defense on the ground that the records are not available and Pahanis for the survey number were stopped being written from 1995 The State Of Telangana And 3 Others vs M/S.Shantha Sriram Constructions ... on 7 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/156916124/

sentences.text: The said observation, admittedly, is the result of consideration of extraneous evidence other than the averments in the plaint and as such is not in consonance with the judicial precedents of the Honourable Apex court.

The Trial Court committed grave error in hinging its conclusions on the solitary contention of the acquisition of land admeasuring Ac.5.10 guntas and Ac.0.05 guntas for laying railway track and for water works pipe line of HMWS, despite the specific explanation in the plaint about non-identity and non-crystallization of localization of the property in respect of which Sri Seth Kishan Ram Gowli claimed compensation without producing any documentary or oral evidence.

However, the Trial Court had surprisingly concluded, without any iota of evidence nor basis, such payment of compensation to be the admission of his right, title and interest over the suit schedule property.

13. The learned Special Government Pleader urged that the Trial Court erred in not considering the five decisions of the Honourable Apex Court AKS,J & VRKR,J CCCA_49_2022 on the point of limitation, though referred and placed before the Trial Court during the course of arguments by the counsel for Appellants/Plaintiffs.

It is respectfully submitted that the reasons adduced and conclusions drawn by the Trial Court were totally based on misconceptions and surmises unsubstantiated by acceptable evidence, more so, the basic premise on which the learned Trial Court have hinged its conclusions basing on the solitary incident of acquisition of land and payment of compensation to Sri Seth Kishan Ram Gowli, without any documentary evidence to prove his title,
per se does not establish the right, title and interest over the suit land of the respondent/Defendant.
A) Submissions on behalf of the respondent/defendant:
14.

Per contra, learned Senior Counsel Sri E. Madanmohan Rao, representing Sri Zeeshan Adnan Mahmood, the learned counsel for the defendant contends that the predecessors-in-title of the defendant have a clear flow of title in their favour of for more than 75 years and have been in long standing possession and enjoyment of the subject land and the same was recognized by the plaintiff State in the revenue records.

15. It is further urged that the Plaintiff State acquired the subject land on two separate occasions by initiating acquisition proceedings and paid compensation to the defendant's predecessors-in-title.

There is no pleading AKS,J & VRKR,J CCCA_49_2022 in the plaint or document filed to show that for the past 76 years the Plaintiff State acted as owner or initiated any steps against the defendant without prescribed period of limitation.

The act of the acquiring part of land from the predecessors-in-title of the defendant is admitted in the plaint, which demonstrates the clear knowledge of the plaintiff State as the very same revenue and Cantonment officials initiated the proceedings, acquired the land and paid compensation to Sri Seth Kishan Ram Gowli, the ancestor through whom the principals/owners who executed the DGPA in favour of the defendant.

Therefore,
from the date of initiation of the land acquisition proceedings, the suit for such relief of cancellation or declaration should have been filed within three years under Article 58 of the Indian Limitation Act.
Hence, the relief of declaration of title on a reading of the plaint itself cannot be countenanced and the same is hopelessly barred by limitation.

The point for adjudication is:
Whether the Trial Court had committed any irregularity or illegality while rejecting the plaint filed by the plaintiffs in O.S.No.55 of 2021 vide the impugned order?
AKS,J & VRKR,J  CCCA_49_2022 VI.

ANALYSIS:
17.

The learned Special Government Pleader contends that the learned Trial Court failed to appreciate that the issue of limitation is a mixed question of law and fact, requiring careful consideration of both the pleadings and the substantial documentary evidence, as well as compliance with binding precedents including the directions of the this Court in W.P.No.5049/2016 and W.A.No.150/2021.

Instead, the Trial Court considered limitation at the threshold under Order VII Rule-11 CPC and did not provide the parties the opportunity to adduce evidence on this material question, resulting in a perverse and illogical order.

In support of the above said contention, the learned Special Government Pleader relied upon decisions in Nusli Neville Wadis v. Ivory Properties and others 3, Vaish Aggarwal Panchayat v. Inder Kumar and others 4, Narne Rama Murthy v.
Ravula Somasndaram and others 5, Ramesh B. Desai and others v. Bipin Vadilal Mehta and others 6 and Shaukathussain Mohammed Patel v. Khatunben Mohmmedbhai Polara7.

In Sopan Sukhdeo Sable v. Asstt. Charity Commissioner13, the Honourable Supreme Court observed that Order VII Rule 11 lays down the legal principle that the plaint 'shall' be rejected if it is barred by any law and the Court has no discretion in this regard and the plaint must be rejected once the bar is apparent from the statement in the plaint itself.

It is further contended by the learned Special Government Pleader that the Trial Court failed to examine and consider the voluminous documentary evidence produced by the plaintiffs which allegedly established a continuous and lawful title for over 75 years, and erroneously (2017) 13 SCC 174 (1986) Supp SCC 315 (2004) 3 SCC 137 AKS,J & VRKR,J CCCA_49_2022 based its conclusions primarily on a single event that the acquisition of a portion of the land and payment of compensation, without proper verification of the plaintiffs' claim of possession and title supported by several government orders and records.

It is pertinent to note that when a suit is liable to be rejected at the budding stage on any of the grounds mentioned in Order VII Rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure, any amount of documentary evidence adduced on behalf of either sides is irrelevant.

In Narbada Devi Gupta v. Birendra Kumar Jaiswal 14, the Honourable Supreme Court observed that mere production and marking of a document as exhibit by the Court cannot be held to be a due proof of its contents.

22. In its findings, the Trial Court emphasized the inadequacy and vagueness of the plaintiffs'
assertions, noting the absence of material particulars or credible documentary evidence capable of establishing any subsisting right or title.

The Court specifically observed that apart from a digital extract of the GLR register, no other document had been advanced to demonstrate the existence of cause of action or lawful interest in the subject property by the plaintiffs, and remarked upon the contradictions (2003) 8 SCC 745 AKS,J & VRKR,J CCCA_49_2022 within the pleadings themselves.

However, it is to be seen that in the case of Madanuri Sri Rama Chandra Murthy v. Syed Jalal 15, the Honourable Apex Court held as under:
"If on an entire and meaningful reading of the plaint, it is found that the suit is manifestly vexatious and meritless in the sense of not disclosing any right to sue, the Court should exercise power under Order VII Rule 11, CPC."

sentences.text: It is settled law that courts have the power and responsibility to summarily dismiss suits at the initial stage if no cause of action or legal right is established.
It is to be seen that cleverly drafted or speculative pleadings cannot create a right to sue if the plaint, as a whole, reveals no genuine cause or substance.
The burden remains with plaintiffs to show substantive right to relief.

25. There is absolutely no doubt that in order to consider an application filed under Order VII Rule 11 of CPC, the averments of the plaint alone have to be taken into consideration and not the pleas taken by the defendants.

The petitioner has mainly contended that the predecessors-in- title of the petitioner have a clear flow of title in their favour for more than 75 years and have been in long standing possession and enjoyment of the subject land and the same was recognized by the respondent/plaintiff state in the records maintained by them and apart from that the respondent/plaintiff state acquired the subject land on two separate occasions by initiating land acquisition proceedings and paying compensation to the petitioner's predecessors-in-title.

On the other hand the respondent/plaintiff State is not denying the fact of acquiring the land of Sri Seth Kishan Ram Gowli, however, submitted that merely because of passing of the award, under misconception and mistaken assumption of AKS,J & VRKR,J CCCA_49_2022 rights, per se, in the absence of authentic relative survey and settlement records does not create any right and title over the property, whose identity, admittedly did not crystallize.

It is to be borne in mind that if the land in question was a government land there was no need for the Plaintiff to initiate land acquisition proceedings and payment compensation to the predecessors-in-title of the defendant.

Furthermore,
there is no record to establish that the Government has preferred any appeal aggrieved by the granting of compensation to defendant's predecessors-in-title.

26. Admittedly, the land belonging to the defendant's predecessors-in- title was acquired by the government twice and compensation was paid twice by passing Awards on 17.05.1985 and 24.06.1989 respectively in favour of Sri Seth Kishan Ram Gowli, who is none other than the defendant's predecessors-in-title in respect of suit schedule property.

Even it is evident that the defendant's predecessors-in-title was in possession and enjoyment of the land vide registered sale deed bearing document No.2230/1955 dated 10.12.1955 to an extent of land admeasuring Ac.56-04 guntas in Sy.Nos.1 & 2, situated at Lothukunta Village.

sentences.text: As per Article 58 of the Limitation Act, the limitation to seek a declaration is only three years from the date when the cause of action arose.

The subject land was acquired by the Government initially in the year 1985 AKS,J & VRKR,J CCCA_49_2022 and the suit of the plaintiff was filed on 30.07.2021 i.e., after a gap of 37 years for declaration of title and permanent injunction and to declare the documents of the defendant and his predecessors-in-title as void documents.

Thus, the respondent/plaintiff having knowledge about the title and possession of Sri Seth Kishan Ram Gowli,
was expected to file the suit within three years from the date of launching land acquisition proceedings of the land situated in the suit schedule property.

The plaintiffs prayed for declaration of the sale deeds pertaining to the year 1995-2006 as void and the said relief is also barred by limitation since such sale deeds and other documents are registered documents prior to 2006.

28. The cause of action paragraph in the plaint discloses that the cause of action initially arose in the year 2013, but the respondent/plaintiff is seeking cancellation of the document for the year 1995-2006.
The Trial Court rightly observed that there is no co-relationship between the cause of action and the prayer of the plaintiffs seeking to declare the documents as void.

As per the proceedings of the Tahsildar, Tirumalgiri Mandal (plaintiff No. 4) under Section 6 of the AP Land Encroachment Act, 1905 vide proceedings No.C/2835/2013 dt.05.12.2013, the defendant was evicted from the suit schedule property, however, such proceedings for eviction initiated by the plaintiff was held as without jurisdiction as per the orders AKS,J & VRKR,J CCCA_49_2022 dated 08.03.2021 passed by the Coordinate Bench of this Court in WP.No. 5049/2016.

In the same order,
the impugned proceedings of Plaintiff Nos.3 & 4 (RDO, Secunderabad division & Tahsildar Tirumalgiri Mandal) in proceeding No.B/3701/2015 dated 13.02.2016 & C/2835/2013 dated 13.11.2015 passed under AP land encroachment Act, 1905 were declared as without jurisdiction, null and void and are set aside; and the plaintiffs herein were directed to restore possession of the land to an extent of Ac.40-00 guntas in Sy.Nos.1 & 2 of Lothkunta Village, which the plaintiffs herein claimed to be in Tirumalgiri Mandal of Hyderabad District, to the defendant herein within four (04)
weeks as plaintiffs took possession of the said land from the defendant pending the disposal of the appeal under Section 10 of the Act by Plaintiff No.3 (RDO, Secunderabad Division).

Further, it was observed that the plaintiff shall not interfere with the possession and enjoyment of the defendant over the said land unless they obtain a decree from a competent civil Court declaring the state's title to the said land, and also a decree for possession against the petitioner/defendant herein and its predecessors-in-title and also imposed costs of Rs.1,00,000/- on the plaintiffs.

Aggrieved by the same, though the plaintiffs preferred W.A.No.150/2021, the operation of the order passed by the learned Single Judge in WP.No.5049/2016 was stayed for a period of four weeks from the date of order passed by the learned Division Bench in W.A.No.150/2021 to AKS,J & VRKR,J CCCA_49_2022 enable the respondents/plaintiffs to approach the Civil Court.
Since the said proceedings of the RDO, Secunderabad and Tahsildar, Tirumalgiri Mandal, which are already set aside in W.P.No.5049/2016, the present suit was filed.

29. The trial Court rightly observed in the impugned order that stay of restoration of possession to the defendant vide W.A.No.150/2021 is for four weeks only from the date of such order and thereafter the plaintiffs are bound to handover possession of the suit property to the defendant as held by the Division Bench in C.M.A.No.535/2021 preferred against the order of status-quo granted by this Court in I.A.No.955/2021 dated 04.10.2021.

sentences.text: But the said proceedings are declared as null and void and the same are set aside by the orders of the learned Single Judge under W.P.No.5049/2016.

Though the plaintiffs sought for cancellation of the sale deeds, the pleadings of the plaint are silent with regard to the date on which the plaintiffs had knowledge about the registered sale deeds of the defendant and his predecessors-in-title.

As stated supra, the defendant and his AKS,J & VRKR,J CCCA_49_2022 predecessors-in-title have flow of title from 10.12.1955, the date on which Sri Seth Kishan Ram Gowli purchased an extent of Ac.59-05 guntas in Sy.Nos.1 & 2, situated at Lothukunta Village from his vendor Smt. Lateefunnisa Begum, W/o. Sri Syed Azmathullah, through her Special Power of Attorney, Sri Syed Mohammed, S/o. Syed Hyder vide Document No.2230/1995.
Even as per Article 112 of the Limitation Act, the period of limitation prescribed is only thirty (30) years from the date of dispossession.
Such period of 30 years is already lapsed in the present case, since the sale deed of Sri Seth Kishan Ram Gowli pertains to 10.12.1955.

The Trial Court while relying on the decision of the Honourable Apex Court in T.Arivandandam Vs. T.V.Satyapal and another 16,
Rajendra Bajoria and others Vs. Hemant Kumar Jalan and others 17, Dahiben's case (supra) opined that the cause of action as stated in the narration of the plaint and the averments specifically under the paragraph dealing with cause of action are at variance.

CONCLUSION:
30.

In the light of the aforesaid discussion, this Court is of the considered opinion that the impugned order passed by the Trial Court is well reasoned and based upon the due appreciation of material available on record.
The appellants failed to show as to how the findings of the Trial Court are illegal and perverse.

31. Therefore, we are of the considered opinion that the plaintiff-State is barred under law of limitation from making a claim contrary to the award passed under land acquisition Act and the same is binding on the plaintiffs, as the said awards remained Unchallenged all these 36 years.
As such, the suit is hopelessly barred by the law of limitation and the same is not maintainable and the plaint is liable to be rejected under Order VII Rule 11 (d) of CPC.

Thus, we are of the opinion that the impugned order does not suffer from any infirmity or illegality and thereby the appellants/plaintiffs failed to establish any of the grounds so as to interfere with the impugned order.
Hence, the appeal is devoid of merits and liable to be dismissed.

15. It is further urged that the Plaintiff State acquired the subject land on two separate occasions by initiating acquisition proceedings and paid compensation to the defendant's predecessors-in-title.
There is no pleading AKS,J & VRKR,J CCCA_49_2022 in the plaint or document filed to show that for the past 76 years the Plaintiff State acted as owner or initiated any steps against the defendant without prescribed period of limitation.
The act of the acquiring part of land from the predecessors-in-title of the defendant is admitted in the plaint, which demonstrates the clear knowledge of the plaintiff State as the very same revenue and Cantonment officials initiated the proceedings, acquired the land and paid compensation to Sri Seth Kishan Ram Gowli, the ancestor through whom the principals/owners who executed the DGPA in favour of the defendant.
Therefore,
from the date of initiation of the land acquisition proceedings, the suit for such relief of cancellation or declaration should have been filed within three years under Article 58 of the Indian Limitation Act.
Hence, the relief of declaration of title on a reading of the plaint itself cannot be countenanced and the same is hopelessly barred by limitation.
The Court specifically observed that apart from a digital extract of the GLR register, no other document had been advanced to demonstrate the existence of cause of action or lawful interest in the subject property by the plaintiffs, and remarked upon the contradictions (2003) 8 SCC 745 AKS,J & VRKR,J CCCA_49_2022 within the pleadings themselves.

Thus,
from the date of initiation of land acquisition proceedings, the suit for such relief of cancellation or declaration, should have been filed within three years under Article 58 of the Limitation Act.
When the right to sue in relation to a suit is based on multiple causes of action, the period of limitation will begin to run from the date when the right to sue first accrues.
Lack of jurisdiction is not a ground for rejection of the plaint and it can be decided after the trial is concluded.
A similar view was taken in Madanuri Sri Rama Chandra Murthy v. Syed Jalal 11.

9 23.
It is settled law that courts have the power and responsibility to summarily dismiss suits at the initial stage if no cause of action or legal right is established.
It is to be seen that cleverly drafted or speculative pleadings cannot create a right to sue if the plaint, as a whole, reveals no genuine cause or substance.
The burden remains with plaintiffs to show substantive right to relief.
25. There is absolutely no doubt that in order to consider an application filed under Order VII Rule 11 of CPC, the averments of the plaint alone have to be taken into consideration and not the pleas taken by the defendants.
It is to be borne in mind that if the land in question was a government land there was no need for the Plaintiff to initiate land acquisition proceedings and payment compensation to the predecessors-in-title of the defendant.
Furthermore,
there is no record to establish that the Government has preferred any appeal aggrieved by the granting of compensation to defendant's predecessors-in-title.
The subject land was acquired by the Government initially in the year 1985 AKS,J & VRKR,J CCCA_49_2022 and the suit of the plaintiff was filed on 30.07.2021 i.e., after a gap of 37 years for declaration of title and permanent injunction and to declare the documents of the defendant and his predecessors-in-title as void documents.
It has been consistently held by the Honourable Supreme Court in catena of decisions that if clever drafting of the plaint has created the illusion of a cause of action, the court will nip it (1977) 4 SCC 467 2021 SCC Online SC 764 AKS,J & VRKR,J CCCA_49_2022 in the bud at the earliest so that bogus litigation will end at the earlier stage.
A similar view was expressed by the Honourable Supreme Court in M/s. Sree Surya Developers and Promoters v. N. Sailesh Prasad and others18. VII.
The appellants failed to show as to how the findings of the Trial Court are illegal and perverse.
31. Therefore, we are of the considered opinion that the plaintiff-State is barred under law of limitation from making a claim contrary to the award passed under land acquisition Act and the same is binding on the plaintiffs, as the said awards remained Unchallenged all these 36 years.
As such, the suit is hopelessly barred by the law of limitation and the same is not maintainable and the plaint is liable to be rejected under Order VII Rule 11 (d) of CPC.
Thus, we are of the opinion that the impugned order does not suffer from any infirmity or illegality and thereby the appellants/plaintiffs failed to establish any of the grounds so as to interfere with the impugned order.
